subject.title: resolveCliAuthEpoch invalidates every live CLI session when local credential source-of-storage flips, even though identity is unchanged

question: For Claude CLI reusable sessions, should an auth epoch track stable credential identity only, or also change when the readable local credential storage source appears or disappears while identity is unchanged?
rationale: Current code intentionally keeps true local credential absence visible, while this issue shows storage-source churn can destroy live session continuity; choosing the boundary changes auth/session policy.

options.title: Prefer stable identity
options.body: Ignore local credential source-presence changes when a selected auth profile already supplies the same identity, while still invalidating on real identity changes and bootstrap credential loss.

options.title: Keep storage-sensitive epochs
options.body: Retain the current conservative invalidation behavior and document that local credential storage changes can reset CLI sessions.

options.title: Adopt backend-owned mode
options.body: Route Claude CLI through a backend ownership mode such as the open host-only proposal if maintainers decide the host credential is the sole auth owner for that runtime.

recommendation.title: Prefer stable identity
recommendation.body: Ignore local credential source-presence changes when a selected auth profile already supplies the same identity, while still invalidating on real identity changes and bootstrap credential loss.

likelyOwner.reason: The earliest and most central CLI OAuth session-continuity commit in the inspected history is by steipete, and the remaining question is the auth/session policy boundary.
